claim: A Censuswide survey fielded in July 2025 and commissioned by Billion Dollar Boy found 52% of content creators (n=1,000, 500 US / 500 UK) have experienced burnout as a direct result of their career.
scope_conditions: Cross-sectional vendor survey of ACTIVE creators recruited by a commercial panel (Censuswide); measures self-reported burnout prevalence among people still working as creators. Cannot sample anyone who has already quit. Not an attrition or survival-rate figure. US/UK only (500 per market); does not generalize to Southeast Asia.
quoted_support: "The study found that more than half (52%) of creators have experienced burnout as a direct result of their career, leading nearly two in five (37%) to actively consider leaving the profession altogether."

claim: 37% of surveyed creators say they 'actively consider leaving the profession altogether' as a result of burnout.
stance_target: documented reasons/intentions creators give for quitting
scope_conditions: Measures STATED INTENTION to quit among active creators still working in the industry at time of survey; by construction the instrument cannot observe whether any respondent subsequently left, and cannot sample creators who already quit. Must never be read as an attrition or exit rate. US/UK only; no Southeast Asia coverage.
quoted_support: "nearly two in five (37%) to actively consider leaving the profession altogether"

claim: Among creators who have experienced burnout, financial instability is the number-one cause when ranked by severity (55%), even though creative fatigue is the most frequently cited cause overall (40%).
stance_target: documented reasons creators give for quitting/burnout
scope_conditions: Severity-ranking question asked only of the subset who reported experiencing burnout, not of all surveyed creators; distinguishes 'most frequently cited' cause from 'most severe' cause - the two are different variables with different denominators. Self-reported, active-creator sample, US/UK only.
quoted_support: "Yet when asked to rank these causes by severity, financial instability emerges as the number one factor (55%) among those who have experienced burnout."

claim: 59% of creators say burnout is negatively impacting their careers, and 58% say it is affecting their overall wellbeing.
scope_conditions: Self-reported impact among active creators; not a measure of actual career exit or reduced output. US/UK only, n=1,000 creators.
quoted_support: "Three in five creators (59%) say it's having a negative impact on their careers, and 58% say it's affecting their overall wellbeing."

claim: Only 48-49% of creators feel adequately supported by brands, agencies, or platforms, versus 60-63% of marketers who believe such support is sufficient - a perception gap between creators and marketers.
stance_target: creator-marketer perception gap on burnout support
scope_conditions: Two separate samples (creators n=1,000, marketers n=1,000) compared; self-reported perceptions, not behavioral or financial data. US/UK only.
quoted_support: "Only around half of creators feel they receive adequate support from brands (48%), agencies (49%) or platforms (49%). By contrast, 60-63% of marketers believe these groups are providing enough support."

claim: The Billion Dollar Boy press release itself does not name Censuswide as the fielding agency, does not state the fieldwork month, and does not disclose the 500/500 US-UK split or the consumer-arm sample sizes - that methodology only survives in a since-shuttered CosmeticsDesign-Europe write-up.
stance_target: methodological transparency of the anchor burnout survey
scope_conditions: Provenance/methodology-audit finding, not a substantive burnout claim. Applies to the primary press release as published at billiondollarboy.com.
quoted_support: "This page does NOT name Censuswide or give fieldwork dates - that methodology statement survives only in the archived CosmeticsDesign-Europe write-up."
